title: innerText for <select>, <optgroup> and <option>
body:
Hi, I'm working to make Blink's innerText to confirm the spec[1].

I found some difficulty to handle <select>, <optgroup> and <option>. Since, in Blink, <select> is implemented in UA shadow root then Blink doesn't have CSS boxes (aka LayoutObject in Blink term) for content in <option>.

In Blink, contents of menu-list (<select size=1>) and list box (<select size=N>) come from
Option#text, which is "label" attribute or <option>.textContents with whitespace collapsion.
In other words, Text node inside <option> never has CSS box.

At this time, I implemented <selection>, <optgroup> to iterate children and uses Option#text to for result item.

In this way, my implementation failed with:
```
<div> in <option> ("<select><option class='poke-div'>123</select>") 
assert_equals: expected "123\nabc" but got "123abc"
```
Note: <div> inside <option> doesn't affect <option>'s label for menu list (<select size="1">), but Firefox shows multiple line <option> item[3].

> option element have an associated non-replaced block-level CSS box whose child boxes are as normal for non-replaced block-level CSS boxes.

To follow this, Blink needs to have yet another implementation of CSS handling for <option>, e.g. :first-line, text-transform, display, and whitespace collapsion. This makes Blink's code complex and having yet another CSS implementation.

Because of inserting <br>, <div> into <option> is unusual and it can be done by script, since parser remove them, it is rare case and it is not worth to have special code for it.

Thus, I proposed to change innerText spec for <select>, <optgroup> and <option> as

- <select> iterator over child nodes, if child is <optgroup> process it, otherwise ignore it.
- <optgroup>: emit one required line break before and start, iterator over child nodes if child is <option>, process it, otherwise ignore it.
- <option>: emit one required line break, emit Option#text, emit one required line break, even if it is outside of <select>


[1] https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#the-innertext-idl-attribute
[2] http://crrev.com/c/1114673 new Element#innerText for Blink
[3] https://jsfiddle.net/Lxo5was9/10/ <option> contains <div>
